description: Heat night. The bedroom (sleep sensor) is 62 F against a 66 F sleep floor while the hallway thermostat is satisfied. The loop raises the thermostat by one 2 F step, the furnace starts within seconds, the loop HOLDS (no second step) while it runs, and steps back to 66 F once the register plume lifts the bedroom reading past target + swing.

events.note: The hallway thermostat's own sensor: satisfied, so it will not start by itself.
Day classification (cold: heat all night / hot: cool all night).
Bedtime: the sleep band is written and the sleep window (remote sensor in use) begins.
The hallway thermostat starts 3 s after the first step (66 -> 68): 'fired -> hold'.
Bedroom still far below target while the furnace runs: hold, NO raise to 70.
Bedroom warming (register plume on the sensor).
Reading passes target + swing (66 + 1.5 = 67.5): step down.
The thermostat stops on its own hysteresis (hallway at its stop point).
Bedroom holds the target for the rest of the hour: no more writes.

assertions.reason: Entering the sleep window starts from NO offset: the plain sleep floor, even though the bedroom is 4 F under it.
THE COMPENSATION: bedroom 62 F is more than the swing under 66 F, so the thermostat is told 66 + one 2 F step so it starts the furnace.
The furnace started within seconds ('fired -> hold'): while it runs and the room is still cold there is NO second step to 70, even though 63.5 F is far under target.
The register plume carries the reading past target + swing (67.6 > 67.5): the offset steps back to zero at once, the thermostat finishes on its own hysteresis.
Bedroom in band for the rest of the hour: no writes at all.

notes: Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md section 10), Issue #1194 increment (e). Tier A: the real ClimateAdvisorCoordinator + AutomationEngine under FakeHass/FakeScheduler (use_coordinator=true, so the sleep-sensor listener and the 1-minute timer are real); every assertion is track=integration for that reason and is evaluated, not skipped.

(a) Effectiveness: scratch-copy mutation run of this scenario against the production code (worktree untouched). It FAILS when M01: the whole offset deleted (the write path adds 0 and the check is a no-op); M07: 'fired -> hold' deleted (a further raise while the equipment runs); M08: the step-down deleted. Passes unmutated.

(b) Docs <-> production alignment: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md 'Remote-sensor outer loop on the thermostat setpoint (Issue #1194, increment a)': rule table rows 'gap > swing / idle / never raised' (RAISE), 'running' (hold, 'fired -> hold' owner decision 2026-11-02), 'gap < -swing, offset > 0' (STEP DOWN). Matches production.
(c) Occupant outcome if this regressed: A person asleep in a bedroom 4 F under their sleep temperature wakes up cold with the furnace never having run.

verdict.summary: Cold bedroom gets the furnace: one 2 F step, hold while it runs, step down at target + swing.
verdict.observed_behavior: 66 F at entry, 68 F one minute later, still 68 F while the furnace runs and the room is cold, 66 F as soon as the reading passes 67.5 F, then silence.
verdict.expected_behavior: The sleeper's room is heated by a thermostat that cannot see it, without the thermostat ever being asked to do more than its own cycle, and the offset does not outstay its welcome.
